what: Dozens of work photo sheets (repeated to reach 30 or more) are lined up in one row like book pages and viewed obliquely from above by an orthographic camera — forming a band that crosses the screen diagonally. One wheel gesture advances one sheet (snapping to the next .15s after release), following eases 4.7% per frame, the advance speed decays ×.829 per frame, and the sheets bend in a sine wave in proportion to that speed. The center sheet pushes its neighbors 4 slots away and rotates (.067, −.363, −.513) rad to face the camera. A hovered side sheet lifts .25 and the center sheet’s photo is pulled in 15.6% (1s power4.out). On entry, 24 sheets flow in with a 2s quartic ease-out and bend heavily, then 1.06s later the center opens (1.1s power2.out).

options.gap: Number of cells the center section pushes neighbors aside, default 4
options.focus: Rotation of the middle sheet in x, y, z (rad), default .06681,-.36331,-.51318
options.decay: Remaining speed share per frame, default .829
options.zoom: Orthographic view height (scene units), default 10.8 — smaller means bigger sections
options.min: Minimum number of sheets to repeat-fill, default 30
options.intro: If off, it stops immediately without drifting off
options.on: If manual, it enters when the consumer sends fx:play to the element (after the loader)
options.[data-fx-part=card]: One section — inside (same source) or note in data-label what the photo is (if absent, a skin-colored placeholder picture)
options.fx:center: When the middle section changes { index, count } — Hang info cards, numbers and color swatches here
options.fx:progress: While flipping, every frame { value (0 to section count, decimals allowed), count } — when the side list flows like the band
options.fx:pick: When you tap the center card { index } — Page transition to the detail page goes here (pressing a neighboring slide brings it to the center)
options.fx:step: Sent to the element, it advances by the detail field (default 1) — arrow buttons, keyboard
options.fx:ready: Rises up once the entrance finishes

use: …
note: The wheel turns sheets instead of scrolling the page while over the strip (preventDefault). Use it on a hero that fills the screen like the original, and when placing it mid long page, let arrows (fx:step) turn the sheets instead of the wheel. The original’s initial stage of sheets rotating and stacking (uProgress) is fixed to 1 in the original and unused, so it was not carried over.
